protocol_deviations: Sequential candidate dispatch (CONCURRENCY vs TOTAL-WORK per issue #27): MAX n bounds total work and fails the run when the list exceeds it; candidates deliberately execute sequentially in collection order instead of dispatching in parallel up to max_workers. This makes USING-any first-success and ranked tie-breaks deterministic by construction, keeps the strict single-IN_PROGRESS ledger invariant, and the required tests pass either way (verified identical event shapes at max_workers 1 and 4). The Wave 10 budget gate still wraps every candidate/judge dispatch (global deadline, per-invocation deadline, slot). Parallel fan-out is future work.

USING-any losers emit no FAILED events while the run can still succeed: audit.py (untouchable) rejects any FAILED event in a run that finishes succeeded (run_finished_status_mismatch). Loser failures are recorded as task_cancelled reason payloads plus the gather task's selection evidence; FAILED events for losers are emitted only in the final all-losers failure batch, keeping every terminal run audit-clean.

The scatter entry's own ledger task stays PENDING while candidates run and starts+completes in the entry's terminal batch: the strict single-in-progress ledger invariant (tasks.py, untouchable) forbids the umbrella task overlapping candidate tasks. The candidates carry the live lifecycle; the scatter's SUCCEEDED (empty delta) marks the entry terminal for the resume prefix invariant and carries the expansion record the gather reads.

External driver (tikhon next/submit, envelope.py) does not support scatter programs: envelope.py is outside this run's allowed file set and rejects IF/CALL programs before plan inspection but has no Scatter branch, so an externally driven scatter program raises AttributeError instead of a clean DriverError. Out of scope for #4.

The draft spec's Reference Program A uses indexed targets (E.urls[Q.part]); indexed targets are a draft-spec feature outside the implemented one-line grammar, so the tested research program uses the unindexed equivalent with candidate-scoped alias.c<k>.<leaf> commits.

The issue text mentions 'all 22 registered commands'; the builtin registry has 17 (calculate, challenge, check, choose, compare, decompose, define, extract, fetch, hypothesize, rank, recall, remember, report, search, summarize, verify). The sealed program uses only registered commands.

GATHER accepts both bare ('GATHER draft AS ...', matching docs/adr/0002) and prefixed ('GATHER step.draft AS ...', matching docs/spec/01) step-id spellings; both normalize and seal identically. The judge step is defined by the indented line following the GATHER (the issue grammar names it via JUDGE step.<id> but does not pin its definition site); this keeps the judge a scoped template that never executes as a plan entry.
